_comment: Third-party modules bot/ imports that are deliberately NOT in
requirements.lock, each with the reason. A ratchet in both directions:
a new entry means somebody added a dependency without pinning it, and an
entry that gets pinned must be deleted in the same commit.
Pillow is NOT in here. It is guarded at all eleven of its import sites,
which made it look optional — and that is exactly how cards vanished on
2026-08-17 with no error. A guarded import means the code SURVIVES the
absence, not that the feature is expendable.
matplotlib, mplfinance and pandas are no longer in here either, and the
entry they left behind is worth reading before adding another. It said:
'Not installed in any environment today, so the chart path has never
run. Pin it or delete the module — but that is a product decision, not a
lockfile one.' Both halves were true and the file sat there for months
while /chart quietly sent text, because a reason written down is not a
decision taken. An entry here is a DEFERRAL, and deferrals need an owner:
say who decides and what the feature does while nobody has.
It also hid behind its own tests. All twenty in test_chart_renderer.py
were skipif'd on the libraries they needed, so the absence rendered as
twenty skips and a green suite. tests/test_no_skip_on_pinned_dependency.py
now refuses that: pinned means a missing module FAILS, declared-optional
means it may skip. Which is to say this file is what tells the two apart,
so a wrong entry here now silences a test suite as well as a feature.

optional.eth_account: EVM transaction signing (bot/web/web3_signer.py). Not installed anywhere; the signer path is unreachable as shipped.
optional.eth_utils: Same module, same status as eth_account.
optional.rlp: Same module, same status as eth_account.
